features.statement: Page title is descriptive, combining brand name with a tagline rather than a short brand abbreviation.
Section titles use h2 headings with a clear heading hierarchy, with h3 reserved for sub-items.
Page content is wrapped in a main landmark element.
Navigation menus are built as semantic ul/li lists.
Includes an accessible hamburger button toggle and ARIA attributes for navigation.
All images carry alt attributes: descriptive for the hero photo, empty for decorative icons.
A full-width hero photograph with a blue color overlay sits below the header.
Uses a system sans-serif font stack instead of the browser default serif.
Hero h1 is a large (about 61px), bold, white tagline wrapping over two lines.
Body text uses generous line height of about 1.6.
Sections alternate background colors between dark navy, white and light grey.
Small uppercase, letter-spaced blue eyebrow labels sit above section headings.
Content is held in a centered container of about 1070px width, not a left-aligned full-width column.
Feature items are arranged in multi-column card grids, such as four across or two side by side.
Cards have slightly rounded corners and subtle borders.
Flat styling with no box shadows, gradients or animations.
Sticky header uses a translucent dark background with backdrop blur and CSS hover transitions.
Header is a dark bar with a letter-spaced bold white wordmark at left and spaced nav links at right.
Primary calls to action are solid blue rectangular buttons; secondary actions are outlined rectangular buttons.
A featured announcement appears as a full-width strip with a blue uppercase badge.
Icons are sized uniformly to about 60px height, white on dark within cards.
News list rows are divided by rules, with large bold day, small uppercase month, headline and right-aligned blue link.
Footer is a dark band with logo and links on one row and copyright below a divider.
Palette is a deliberate navy, bright blue and white scheme with light-grey accents.
Nav and list links are not underlined and are colored by context; only inline links stay underlined.
Page ships without external scripts or stylesheets, with minimal head metadata.
No social icon glyphs or icon fonts; header and footer use text-only links.
Dates and eyebrow labels are CSS-uppercased, and Read More links and banners get trailing arrows.
News headlines are medium-weight sans-serif h4 headings.
